name: Tree Green
lede: Tree Green is a saturated, mid-dark [[green]] close to the Xbox brand's logo color, with its own origin undocumented in our sources.

sections.title: Origin undocumented
sections.body:
Our graph marks the origin of Tree Green as undocumented: it is recorded by the 2010 xkcd crowd survey and separately noted on Wikipedia, but neither source explains who coined the pairing or when [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for it reads "deep yellowish green" [1].

Wikipedia's entry for this hex notes it as a near-duplicate, about 2.3 units off by CIEDE2000, of the green used in the Xbox brand's logo [1]. Nearby names in our library are [[forest-green|Forest Green]], [[grass-green|Grass Green]] and [[kelly-green|Kelly Green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Tree Green is one of the rarer matches in our archive, covering at least 2% of the canvas in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. By position in each painting's lightness order it is found in just 1, rarer than 86% of the named colors we track [2]. Where it does appear, it always sits as a shadow, not a highlight [2].

In printed English, "tree green" as a phrase peaked in the 1870s and rose fastest that same decade, well before the xkcd survey's 2010 record for this exact hex [2].

questions.q: What does our data say about who coined the name Tree Green?
choices: It is undocumented in our sources
A paint company trademarked it in the 1950s
It first appears in Ridgway's 1912 book
questions.answer: It is undocumented in our sources
